title: Forward coordinates for already free integral sheet modules
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite-dimensional totally disconnected normed Q_l-extension E, and A=continuousIntegers(l,E) [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Let p:U\to X and g:Y\to X be arbitrary scheme morphisms, P an internal continuous E-module on X, M an internal continuous A-module on U, and e:Ext(M)\cong p*P. Let d be any natural number and t_j:Y\to U with t_j p=g. Suppose g*P and every t_j*M are globally finite free internal modules. Then there are a rank r and functions G_j:|Y|\to GL_r(E) with continuous entries and inverse entries. For every open W\subseteq Y there are continuous-function presentations [def-sfb-continuous-function-module-presentation] c of Res((g|W)*P) by E^r and b_j of (t_j|W)*M by A^r. For every pro-etale B over W, section x of the encoded integral module, and z\in |B|, c(f_j(x))(z)=G_j(z)b_j(x)(z), where f_j is the actual normalized finiteEtaleLatticeSheetEmbedding [def-sfb-finite-etale-lattice-sheet-maps]. No finite-etale, surjectivity, splitting, positive-degree, covering, range or locally constant coset assertion is made.

proof.text: Apply continuousFreeSheet_globalCoordinates to obtain the rational rank r, independent integral ranks n_j, global presentations c,b_j, and natural E-linear coordinate equivalences F_{j,B} satisfying the normalized global sheet equation.

The private theorem natural_linear_map_matrix constructs each rectangular continuous matrix by applying F at the terminal pro-etale object to constant basis vectors. Expand every vector-valued continuous function as a finite sum of its coordinate functions times these basis vectors. Linearity and naturality give the formula on every test object. Apply the same construction to F inverse; the composite identities evaluated on constant basis vectors give two-sided rectangular inverse identities. These steps are proved in Lean in the item.

If Y has a point, evaluate the rectangular inverse identities there. Their mulVec linear maps give an E-linear equivalence, so LinearEquiv.finrank_eq and Module.finrank_fin_fun imply n_j=r. Substitute this equality and package the two evaluated matrices as units in the square matrix ring. Both matrices have continuous entries because their entries are the global continuous coefficient functions just constructed. If Y is empty, every test object is empty; the private empty_presentation_rank transports the integral presentations to rank r using the unique additive equivalence between their continuous-function spaces, and choose identity matrices. This proves the entire rank, matrix, continuity, inverse and empty-base part without further admitted statements.

Use the global coordinate equation and the proved matrix action formula to get c(f_j(x))(z)=G_j(B.hom(z))b_j(x)(z). Apply continuousSheet_coordinate_restriction to this equation. It supplies the required presentations and exact normalized formula on every open W.

theorem continuousFreeSheet_frames
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type) [NormedField E]
    [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace E] {X U Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X))
    (p : U ⟶ X)
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff l E) U))
    (e : (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap l E) U)).obj M ≅
      (upperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) p).obj P)
    (g : Y ⟶ X) (d : ℕ) (t : Fin d → (Y ⟶ U)) (w : ∀ j, t j ≫ p = g)
    (hP : Mod.IsFree (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) Y)
      ((upperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) g).obj P))
    (hM : ∀ j, Mod.IsFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff l E) Y)
      ((upperStar (integralCoeff l E) (t j)).obj M)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (G : Fin d → Y → Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin r) E),
      (∀ j i k, Continuous (fun y ↦ (G j y).val i k)) ∧
      (∀ j i k, Continuous (fun y ↦ ((G j y)⁻¹).val i k)) ∧
      ∀ W : Y.Opens, ∃ w' : ∀ j, (W.ι ≫ t j) ≫ p = W.ι ≫ g,
        ∃ c : ContinuousFunctionPresentation W.toScheme (continuousIntegers l E)
            (Fin r → E) ((Mod.comap
              (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap l E) W.toScheme)).obj
              ((upperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) (W.ι ≫ g)).obj P)),
        ∃ b : ∀ j, ContinuousFunctionPresentation W.toScheme (continuousIntegers l E)
            (Fin r → continuousIntegers l E)
            ((upperStar (integralCoeff l E) (W.ι ≫ t j)).obj M),
        ∀ (j : Fin d) (B : W.toScheme.ProEt)
          (x : ((continuousRingModuleEquivalence W.toScheme
            (continuousIntegers l E)).functor.obj
            ((upperStar (integralCoeff l E) (W.ι ≫ t j)).obj M)).val.obj (op B))
          (z : B.left),
          c.sections B
            (((continuousRingModuleEquivalence W.toScheme
              (continuousIntegers l E)).functor.map
              (finiteEtaleLatticeSheetEmbedding (integralScalarMap l E) P p M e
                (W.ι ≫ g) (W.ι ≫ t j) (w' j))).val.app (op B) x) z =
            (G j (W.ι (B.hom z))).val *ᵥ
              (fun i ↦ ((b j).sections B x z i : E))
